invariants.evidence: Deterministic check `python3 tools/verify_p2.py r2-series` exited 0 with no violation output. Corroborating read of adspend.json: all five named series are present with declared two-element coverage windows -- coen_mce [1919,2007] 1197 points, magna [1980,2025] 9 points, iab_pwc [1996,2025] 35 points, irs_soi [1960,2022] 19 points, benchmarks_pre1919 [1867,1918] 9 points. The verifier also asserts every point's source_series tag matches its containing series and that year and value are present.

Deterministic check `python3 tools/verify_p2.py r2-concordance` exited 0 with no violation output. The check builds a (year, medium) occupancy map across all series and requires a concordance entry for every pair that co-occupies a cell, requires bridge.window/method/arithmetic to be non-empty, and requires every point flagged bridged:true to carry calibration.grade == "C". Corroborating read: 19 concordance entries present; all 28 bridge_mce_mg8 points carry bridged:true and grade C.

Deterministic check `python3 tools/verify_p2.py r2-checks` exited 0 with no violation output. cross_checks holds 31 entries; no entry carries |divergence_pct| > 15 while flagged is false. All 4 forecasts in forecasts.json carry 3 panelists (>= the required 3) plus both median and variance: fc-total-adspend-001 (median 440, var 10.666667), fc-digital-share-001 (median 76, var 0.086667), fc-retail-media-001 (median 71.5, var 0.388889), fc-search-001 (median 129.5, var 2.722222). See contract_concerns[0]: the contracted command does not test the invariant's 'every overlap year' clause, and 1960 appears to be an uncovered overlap year.

Judgment check against the two failure modes the contract names. (1) 'Says differs without magnitude': no such entry. All 19 concordance entries carry a populated magnitude object (2-7 keys). The billings-vs-revenue basis difference is decomposed numerically in coen-magna-basis: 1980 MCE $53,570m vs MG8 $41,021m, raw_level_break_pct_1980 -23.43, like_for_like_wedge_pct_1980 -7.21, scope_share_of_break_pct 69.2. Category scope changes carry both year and magnitude -- coen-ooh-2000 (ooh_1999 $4,780m vs billboards_1999 $1,725m, ratio 2.771), coen-category-lifecycle (Yellow Pages enters 1980 at $2,900m against a miscellaneous step of -$2,074m), coen-tv-split-1990 (identity_residual_musd 0), coen-medium-detail-1935 (other_share_of_1919_total_pct 62.6). The three thinnest entries still carry hard numbers (iab-vintage max_restatement_pct 0.19; bridge-vs-coen -23.4/-17.4 pct; naa-online-2003 $3,166m, 14.9% of IAB). The one entry marked "status": "unquantified" (magna-basis-change) does not violate the instruction: it names precisely what differs (direct mail possibly leaving the MG8 basis), supplies both dollar anchors (mg8_2018_musd 232906, us_direct_mail_scale_for_reference_musd 60225) and a numeric bound ('roughly 10-15% of total'), and states why an exact figure is unavailable (the methodology document is licensed and was not read). That is a disclosed epistemic limit with a quantified bound, not an unquantified 'differs'. (2) 'Bridge estimated outside its overlap window': not the case. coen_mce spans 1919-2007 and magna spans 1980-2025, so the series overlap is exactly 1980-2007; bridge.window is [1980,2007] and all 28 bridge_mce_mg8 points fall inside it with none outside. bridge.gaps_not_bridged explicitly declines to bridge 2008-2020 and 2011-2025 where no overlap exists, leaving those holes visible -- the discipline the invariant is protecting. All 10 entries in bridge.steps re-evaluate to their stored expected values within 1e-9 (W = 41021/44207 = 0.9279299658425136 reproduces exactly). The single-observation weakness is foregrounded rather than concealed: overlap_observations is declared as 1, wedge.held_constant true with why_constant, known_direction_of_error states the true wedge is probably below 0.928 in the 2000s, and the ci80 on bridge points resolves to exactly [0.85, 0.98] of the restricted base at both 1980 and 2007, matching the documented skew. An out-of-sample check at 2007 against GroupM's published US measured-media total gives -0.52%, carrying the caveat that GroupM 'bounds the bridge, it does not confirm it'. dataset-notes.md section 6 repeats the same admission in prose: 'a wedge constant across 27 years on one observation is the weakest link in this dataset and is graded C everywhere'.

Deterministic check `python3 tools/verify_p2.py r2-reconcile` exited 0 with no violation output. The check compares era SCALE dollar-total claims (normalised to millions USD, skipping percent/share/change/world claims as category errors) against assembled totals from benchmarks_pre1919, coen_mce and magna, using each claim's own ci80 as tolerance. It carries an explicit anti-vacuity guard that raises a violation if zero claims could be compared; that guard did not fire, so the reconciliation was actually exercised rather than trivially passing on an empty comparison set.

Deterministic check `python3 tools/verify_p2.py r2-freeze` exited 0 with no violation output. The check rejects any sourced point in adspend.json with year > 2025 and any point whose calibration.as_of exceeds the freeze date. Corroborating read: the maximum year across all adspend.json series points is 2025 (magna, iab_pwc), and the post-freeze projections live in forecasts.json as 4 forecast objects. See contract_concerns[1] on the proxy nature of the year test.

contract_concerns.concern: The contracted command is materially weaker than the invariant text it enforces, and there is concrete evidence the untested clause does not hold. The invariant requires that 'The IRS cross-check is computed for every year where irs_soi overlaps the assembled totals'. The command's implementation (tools/verify_p2.py, r2_checks, lines 249-266) only iterates cross_checks entries that already exist and flags any with |divergence_pct| > 15 that are not marked flagged; it never verifies coverage. Observed gap: irs_soi carries 19 year-points (1960, then 2005-2022) but cross_checks covers 2005-2022 only among IRS years, leaving 1960 with no entry. 1960 has both an irs_soi point ($9,291m) and an assembled coen_mce total ($11,960m), which would yield a divergence of -22.3% -- past the 15% tolerance and therefore requiring flagged:true. The audit verdict above records the contracted command's result as the contract directs; this concern is raised separately so the pipeline owner can decide whether to tighten the check or add the 1960 entry.

The check self-documents as a proxy. tools/verify_p2.py line 339 reads '# PROXY: annual points for 2026+ belong in forecasts.json, not adspend.json', implementing the 2026-06-30 freeze date as a year > 2025 test on point years. For annual-resolution data this is a defensible proxy, and the check does additionally compare calibration.as_of against the literal freeze date, so the gap is narrow. Noted only so the substitution is on the record rather than implicit.
